messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of reconnects from a handful of customers after a graceful server shutdown. They look like probe loops vs normal client retries.
priya: Saw that too. Symptoms? high reconnect rate for ~30s after the close, extra token billing, and console shows route churn.
mateo: Logs show server sending 499/close-with-reason, clients immediately reauth and open a new WS -> backend creates new session before old tombstones expire. Quota window double-counting.
jin: Repro steps: curl a close -> client lib does exponential backoff but first few steps are near-instant. Our quota calculator treats each new session as fresh usage until tombstone TTL.
sara: Can we differentiate graceful-close probes from actual new sessions in routing/telemetry? maybe a short-lived probe flag? :thinking_face:
alex: Idea: set a short header on server close: `X-Session-Closed: graceful` and surface it through the proxy so routing can mark the following reconnects as "probing" for 5s and not charge/bill in full.
priya: Hmm risky for abuse. Clients could set that header. Server needs to be authoritative. Only the server (our runtime) should emit it, proxy must trust internal header from edge -> backend.
mateo: Implementation sketch: on graceful shutdown, emit `x-ri-close: graceful:<session-id>` on upstream close. Proxy keeps a small LRU of recent session-ids for dedupe for 10s. Telemetry tags requests with `probe=true` when matching.
jin: Also need console UX: show "post-close probes" on the route dashboard so Customer Success can explain billing blips. Right now customers see repeated short sessions and freak out.
sara: Agreed. A couple of questions: 1) Does this fix billing or just telemetry? 2) Do we break SLA counting if we suppress charges?
alex: 1) Initially telemetry + dedupe for quota accounting for N seconds. 2) We can keep SLA metrics unchanged (count incoming connections) but apply a discounted unit-cost for probe-tagged tokens.
priya: Another angle: teach client libs to respect `Retry-After` or `Connection: close` semantics and add jitter. But we can't rely on all clients. So server-side is safer.
mateo: We should also add a conservative server-side cooldown: after graceful close, NAP (no-auth-probe) for 2s where auth attempts get 202/try-later to slow down clients. That avoids immediate reauth storms.
jin: 202 could confuse some clients. Maybe return `429` with `Retry-After` 2s for auth endpoints only. Keep streaming handshake separate.
sara: For rollout: feature flag behind `platform.probe-dedupe-v1`, enable for a tiny % of traffic, monitor billing delta and reconnect rate. Also add an on-console toggle per-tenant to opt-in.
alex: Telemetry: add `probe_reason` tag (`graceful_shutdown`, `proxy-restart`, `failed-migrate`) and a dashboard that shows count, avg tokens per probe, and estimated cost delta.
priya: I can draft a small proposal with sequence diagram + perf implications. Will ping infra for memory hit on LRU cache.
mateo: FYI deploy-bot: deploy of proxy change will need coordinated rollout to edge and runtime to emit header.
deploy-bot: CI passed for proxy dedupe spike detection. Staging rollout scheduled for 2026-03-22 03:00 UTC.
jin: Follow-ups: (a) small LRU + leak proofing, (b) conservative default probe TTL=5s, (c) console telemetry + billing experiment, (d) client lib guidance in docs.
sara: ok. Priya + Mateo take ownership for rollout plan. Alex to file console ticket. I'll coordinate CS comms.
priya: On it — will post draft in #eng-platform tomorrow.
mateo: I'll prototype the header and LRU in a small PR and attach telemetry mocks.
alex: Thanks team. If we catch a customer hit in the wild, we can toggle per-tenant immediately.
priya: One more: add a short note in the Runtime API docs about the `x-ri-close` header being internal-only. Don't expose as stable public contract.
sara: sounds good :+1:
